attestation.summary: 1 CRITICAL (verify-log endpoint broken), 1 HIGH (weak default HMAC key), 2 MEDIUM (retention & rotation not implemented). Core HMAC-SHA256 signing and tamper detection logic is correct, but operational readiness is compromised by the critical functional bug and security-sensitive key management default. All findings independently confirmed by both verifiers with no contradictions.

findings.detail: 5 event types: all required fields present in audit.py _REQUIRED_FIELDS + auto-injected event_type/log_id/timestamp. app.py extracts all per-event fields correctly.
Universal fields (event_type, log_id) auto-injected on every log_event() call.
UUID4 log_id via uuid.uuid4(); 100-call uniqueness test passes.
Canonical JSON: sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False, signature excluded before signing.
verify_log() detects: missing signature, tampered fields, replaced signature, mixed valid/tampered. Returns correct indices (when called with correct arguments). 0 false positives, 0 false negatives.
Boundary conditions: empty strings, Unicode, extra fields, deterministic/order-invariant signatures all handled correctly.

app.py L160: audit.verify_log() called without required 'entries' argument. /verify-log endpoint always fails with TypeError: verify_log() missing 1 required positional argument: 'entries'. Fix: audit.verify_log(audit.get_log()).
Retention policy (7 years / 2555 days) not implemented. In-memory _log_store provides no persistence or archival.
Log rotation (daily, audit_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl) not implemented. No file-based storage exists.
get_log() returns shallow copy — returned list is new but dict elements are same references as store. Low risk for verification use cases.

AUDIT_HMAC_KEY defaults to hardcoded 'default-key' when environment variable is unset. An attacker who knows this default can forge valid signatures for arbitrary audit entries, rendering tamper detection ineffective in deployments where AUDIT_HMAC_KEY is not explicitly configured. Recommend: use os.environ['AUDIT_HMAC_KEY'] (fail-fast on missing) or generate a random key at startup with a warning.

HMAC-SHA256 signing implementation verified: sort_keys=True ensures canonical field ordering; compact separators (',',':') produce deterministic output; ensure_ascii=False handles Unicode correctly; signature field is excluded from signing payload (computed before attachment in log_event()); hmac.compare_digest() provides constant-time comparison guarding against timing side-channels.

4 attack vectors tested — signature stripping (entry.get('signature') → None → tampered), signature replacement (compare_digest mismatch → tampered), field value tampering (altered canonical JSON → mismatch), extra field injection (alters canonical JSON → mismatch). All correctly detected.

All 5 business endpoints (/config-changed, /user-login, /report-accessed, /data-exported, /payment-initiated) correctly call audit.log_event() with proper field mappings. Each call is wrapped in try/except Exception → logger.warning, ensuring audit failures never block business responses. Route signatures and return structures are unchanged.
app.py L160: audit.verify_log() called without required 'entries' argument. Consistent with V1-F07 — cross-verifier confirmation of the same blocking defect.

Cross-verifier consistency check: all findings from verifier1 and verifier2 are mutually consistent with no contradictions. The critical defect (V1-F07 / V2-F05) is independently confirmed by both verifiers.

action_items.action: Replace hardcoded default HMAC key 'default-key' with mandatory environment variable or auto-generated random secret
Implement log persistence and archival mechanism for 7-year retention compliance
Implement daily log rotation with audit_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl file naming
